node-1.label: A 49-year-old woman has facial ulcers, including healed lower lip and nasal dorsum ulcers and a nonhealing left infraorbital ulcer

node-2.label: Patient reported several years of facial ulcers described as 'scratches' developing over weeks to months into red, indurated, tender ulcers that finally crusted and healed; healed ulcers were present on the lower lip and nasal dorsum, with a nonhealing ulcer in the left lateral infraorbital area

node-3.label: Review of systems was positive for dry mouth, Raynaud phenomenon, morning joint pain, mild hand and ankle swelling, and dysphagia

node-4.label: Later examination revealed diplopia, a sense of fullness below the left eye, restriction of the left eye into hypotropic and exotropic positions, full-thickness defect through the lateral lower eyelid, and exposed conjunctiva and bony orbital rim

attrs.why: Positive ANA, low C4, elevated ACE, saddle nose, and systemic symptoms still support an autoimmune/vasculitic process. However, the pathologist and radiologist interpret the polarizable foreign-body granulomas and MRI hypointense mass as exogenous inflammation, and they note that the autoimmune findings and saddle nose are nonspecific and could be secondary. Since exhaustive history retrieval found no trauma, injection, or exposure source, autoimmune/vasculitic disease remains a residual secondary consideration; confidence is therefore reduced from 0.40 to 0.35.

Pathologist analysis emphasizes that negative cultures exclude infection, and the orbital biopsy showing polarizable foreign-body granulomas is not consistent with an infectious process. The systemic sicca, Raynaud phenomenon, and arthralgia are atypical for primary infection. MRI hypointense mass further argues against an abscess or infectious mass. Confidence is reduced from 0.08 to 0.05.

The orbital biopsy shows granulomatous inflammation with polarizable foreign material rather than malignant cells, and expert analyses confirm that the MRI hypointense mass and biopsy findings refute malignancy. The chronic multifocal ulcer course with systemic symptoms also makes neoplasm unlikely. Confidence is reduced from 0.05 to 0.03.
